chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: “Indeed, in the Jafr which they mention, there is that which displeases them, because they do not speak the truth, while the truth is in it.”

So let them bring forth the judgments of Ali and his ordinances, if they are truthful; and ask them about the maternal aunts and the paternal aunts; and let them bring forth the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام), for indeed in it is the bequest of Fatimah (عليها السلام), and with it are the weapons of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Bring a book before this, or a trace of knowledge, if you are truthful.”

key_terms.أَثَارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ: A trace or remnant of knowledge offered as proof.
key_terms.الْجَفْرِ: The Jafr, a repository mentioned as containing true knowledge.
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: The truth, which the Imam (عليه السلام) says is contained therein.
key_terms.سِلَاحُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The weapons of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), mentioned as accompanying it.
key_terms.فَرَائِضَهُ: His prescribed ordinances or legal obligations.
key_terms.قَضَايَا عَلِيٍّ: The judicial rulings or judgments of Ali (عليه السلام).
key_terms.مُصْحَفَ فَاطِمَةَ: The Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام), identified here as containing her bequest.
key_terms.وَصِيَّةَ فَاطِمَةَ: The bequest or testament of Fatimah (عليها السلام).

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe al-Jafr and the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام) as proofs of knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the presence of authoritative knowledge in the inherited sacred materials associated with the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), including al-Jafr and the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام). It challenges false claims to such knowledge by calling for demonstrable legal and inherited proofs, and it concludes by invoking a Qur'anic demand for authentic textual or transmitted evidence.
